reply.text:
Think of bracing as making a tight, pressurized cylinder out of your midsection before you unrack the bar.

Take a breath in through your nose and send it into your belly and sides, not your chest, as if you're filling a belt around your waist. Then tighten your abs and obliques like you're about to take a punch, and keep that air and tension locked in while you squat down and stand back up. Let the air out only at the top, then reset with a fresh breath for the next rep.

Two common mistakes: breathing up into your chest, which lifts the ribs and arches the lower back, and letting the air leak out at the bottom of the rep. A lifting belt can give you something to push your abs against, but learn to brace without one first.

If you want, film a set and I can check it with you in the form check.
